title: Post-incident: SLA violations from autoscale regression; runbook and policy hardening
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Summary: On 2026-03-10 between 02:55–03:40 UTC Redwood Dedicated experienced a capacity shortfall that caused sustained SLA breaches (increased p95 and p99 tail latency, and several 503s) for customers on two reserved pools. The immediate trigger was an autoscaling regression introduced as part of runtime autoscale tuning (runtime-1.19 rollout) that incorrectly tightened the scale-up threshold for nodes handling long-sequence workloads, preventing sufficient pod/GPU provisioning under burst load. This ticket contains the timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and a prioritized set of follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-10 02:48 UTC: Canary telemetry shows slight increase in response latency on dedicated-pool-A; alert thresholds not yet breached.
2026-03-10 02:55 UTC: Automated p95 latency alert fires for dedicated-pool-A; on-call engineer paged (Incident #RID-2026-0310-1).

2026-03-10 03:02 UTC: Investigation reveals scale-up events are not occurring despite rising queue depth; autoscaler logs show scale decisions suppressed due to new 'stability window' logic from runtime-1.19.

2026-03-10 03:10 UTC: Emergency rollback of runtime-1.19 autoscale patch to previous stable branch initiated; temporary increase of burst capacity applied to both affected pools (manual override + add-capacity script).
2026-03-10 03:28 UTC: Latency begins to recover; p95 returns to SLO-boundary but p99 still elevated for another 30 minutes as KV caches warm and queued work drains.
2026-03-10 03:40 UTC: Incident declared resolved; retrospective and postmortem started.
root_cause_summary: A change in the autoscaler logic that introduced a longer 'stability window' plus an off-by-one bug in the threshold evaluation for long-sequence inference caused the autoscaler to ignore legitimate scale-up signals under bursty workloads. Two contributing factors: 1) insufficient synthetic load tests for long-sequence distributions in pre-release canary; 2) missing alert mapping that should have escalated queue-depth anomalies separate from latency alerts.
immediate_mitigations: Rolled back autoscaler commit (runtime-1.19 -> runtime-1.18 autoscale behavior) across affected Dedicated pools (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1124).
Applied manual burst-capacity override to reserved pools for customer-facing tiers (internal runbook script: /confluence/dedicated/runbooks/overrides).

Opened high-priority telemetry dashboard to track queue depth, scale decisions, and cold-start time across all dedicated pools (Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd123/dedicated-autoscale).
long_term_actions: Revert and rework the stability-window autoscale feature; add canary gating for long-sequence workloads with synthetic traffic that matches customer distributions (owner: infra-autoscale team; ETA: 2 sprints).
Add a dedicated alert mapping: separate queue-depth anomalies from latency SLOs and escalate queue-depth on dedicated pools to on-call immediately (owner: observability; ETA: 1 sprint).

Introduce pre-release integration tests that run end-to-end scale-up scenarios for long-sequence models and multi-tenant traffic shapes before merging autoscaler changes (owner: runtime QA; ETA: 3 sprints).

Create a policy for automatic temporary capacity borrowing between compatible reserved pools as a short-term mitigation when one pool experiences a localized burst (owner: capacity-ops; ETA: RFC 2 weeks).
Expand our canary traffic mix to include curated customer prompt sets and sequence length distributions used by the top 10% of dedicated customers (owner: product & applied-ml; ETA: 4 weeks).
action_items: AI-1: infra-autoscale to implement a fixed-mode that preserves pre-1.19 scaling thresholds and publish a toggle (assignee: Aisha Kapoor; due: 2026-03-18).
AI-2: Observability to add queue-depth escalation rule and playbook step that routes to incident commander (assignee: Priya Desai; due: 2026-03-17).
AI-3: QA to add a long-sequence synthetic workload scenario to the pre-merge pipeline and a nightly stress test (assignee: Daniel O'Neil; due: 2026-03-31).
AI-4: Capacity team to define capacity-borrow policy and run tabletop drill for cross-pool borrowing (assignee: Sofia Martinez; due: 2026-04-01).
AI-5: Docs to update Dedicated runbook with a clear rollback checklist, command snippets, and escalation matrix (assignee: Ben Thompson; due: 2026-03-20).
postmortem_summary: Impact: ~18 minutes of sustained p95/p99 increases, 12 customer-facing 503s across two reserved pools, and a temporary violation of tiered throughput guarantees for three enterprise customers. Root cause: autoscale logic regression + insufficient test coverage for long-sequence workloads. We mitigated by rollback and temporary manual capacity. Preventative measures include additional alerts, stronger canary tests, and a capacity-borrow policy. The incident highlights the need for workload-tailored canaries and clearer observability for autoscale decisions.
